name: Balanced 4-1-2-1-2 Diamond

slots.why: Distributes to a compact team; the short passing game does not need a sweeper.
Primary source of width on this side. Wing-Back (Support) is preferred because the diamond has no winger; Full-Back (Support) is the more conservative alternate.
Central defender in a narrow, compact block. Cover is the alternate.
Central defender on the right of the pair. Cover is the alternate, but at most one of the two can be Cover.
Primary source of width on this side. Wing-Back (Support) is preferred because the diamond has no winger; Full-Back (Support) is the more conservative alternate.
Holding midfielder is the base of the diamond and shields the centre-backs.
Provides the main midfield running from the side of the diamond, shuttling between phases and joining attacks while the DM and DLP provide structure.
Deep-lying playmaker receives from the defensive unit and controls progression through the compact midfield.
Operates between the lines as the advanced central creator, combining with both strikers and the midfield behind him.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) links the attacking midfielder to the other striker.
Second striker runs in behind, using the space the other forward creates. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A compact narrow 4-1-2-1-2 built around central combinations, a holding midfielder, a distributor, a midfield runner and an attacking midfielder, with the wide defenders supplying almost all of the width.
whyGood: It creates central numerical superiority while giving the midfield four distinct jobs: the DM anchors, the DLP progresses possession, the Box-to-Box midfielder adds vertical running, and the AMC creates behind two complementary strikers.
whyThisShape: The diamond overloads the centre with a holding midfielder, a deep distributor, an end-to-end runner and an attacking midfielder. A support forward links those players to a second striker attacking depth. Because there are no wingers, the wide defenders must provide the outside outlet.
whenToUse: When your strongest players are central, you can field two complementary strikers, and your wide defenders are capable of supplying the width the shape otherwise lacks.
whenNotToUse: When the opposition can isolate your wide defenders repeatedly, when your wide defenders cannot cover the flank athletically, or when your central players are not secure enough to combine in congested areas.

instructionRationale.Fairly Narrow: Fits the diamond, where the four central players work in tight combinations.
instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Short triangles in the middle are the diamond's strength.
instructionRationale.Counter: The diamond can win the ball in the centre and break quickly through the two strikers.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Drops back into shape after losing the ball; a narrow shape has to stay compact.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: A balanced press: engages when the ball enters the compact block rather than chasing wide.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: A balanced line keeps the team compact without exposing the centre-backs.

keyRequirements: Wide defenders capable of providing the formation's width repeatedly
A disciplined holding midfielder at the base of the diamond
A reliable deep distributor and an energetic midfield runner
An attacking midfielder comfortable receiving and creating in congested central areas
A linking forward paired with a striker who threatens the space beyond
